title: Climate-response models in 11 families kept little skill over a trailing mean with only weather known at the forecast date (26,103 series, 2005-2024); a lead-aware false-signal rate showed this
abstract: Question: which climate-response relations keep forecast skill when a model can use only the weather that is known at the forecast date? Earlier campaign tests used observed target-year weather. Approach: we rebuilt 11 families (river flow, lake ice, cherry and German plant and crop phases, birds, river invertebrates, NDVI, dengue, crop yields; 26,103 series) with unchanged code and reproduced the published results exactly. We froze a timestamped plan, then refitted the same engine with windows that end 0-12 months before the end of the reference month and forecast 2005-2024 against a 5-year trailing mean. Results: the four families with strong perfect-prognosis gains (0.34-0.65) kept 78-102% at lead 1, but lead 1 was a median 7-15 days before the event and 20-33% of events had already occurred. At lead 2 (37-45 days ahead) gains fell to 0.07 for ice and to 0 or below elsewhere; annual river flow had no gain before the year started. With this strict lead, no rule beat the trailing mean (difference -0.0015, 95% interval -0.0026 to 0.0008). A false-signal rate computed with issue-time windows rose with lead, ordered forward skill (rho -0.56, p = 0.0001) and chose correctly in 87% of 39 cells (class rule 51%). A lead-aware gate beat a lead-blind gate (+0.016, 0.011 to 0.024). Keeping the published model and filling missing months with recent climatology beat refitting (+0.078) and was best overall. Limitations: no weather or seasonal forecasts tested; monthly leads; single-window linear models; 11 families; one post-freeze NaN fix.
